proposals.before: After Liu Bei brought Shu under control, Dong He was called up as general of the household for army affairs and, alongside Military Director-in-Chief Zhuge Liang, jointly ran the Left General and grand marshal’s headquarters—offering candid counsel and enjoying genuine rapport.
proposals.after: After Liu Bei brought Shu under control, Dong He was called up as general of the household for army affairs and, alongside Army Advisor General Zhuge Liang, jointly ran the Left General and grand marshal’s headquarters—offering candid counsel and enjoying genuine rapport.
proposals.reason: 軍師將軍 is the Army Advisor / Director-General office, not 'Military Director-in-Chief'.

proposals.before: I would blush before the maxim ‘to possess yet seem empty, to be full yet seem modest’—I cannot accept this honor!"〉"
proposals.after: I would blush before the maxim ‘to possess yet seem empty, to be full yet seem modest’—I cannot accept this honor!"
proposals.reason: Trailing extra quotes after the commentary closer are artifacts, not part of the translated reply.

proposals.before: Liu Bei soon seized three southern commanderies, cutting off Liu Ba’s return route, so he fled far south toward Jiaozhi.
proposals.after: When the First Sovereign came to hold roughly the three commanderies, Ba could not return from his mission, so he went far off toward Jiaozhi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 巴不得反使 means Ba could not return from the envoy mission, not that Liu Bei cut a return route; the idiomatic sentence invents a causal military cutoff.

proposals.before: From Jiaozhi Liu Ba eventually made his way into Shu.
proposals.after: From Jiaozhi, Liu Ba eventually made his way into Shu.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place-name Jiaozhi with the person-name Liu Ba and obscures the travel sequence.

proposals.before: During the siege of Chengdu Liu Bei ordered: "Anyone who harms Liu Ba will answer with the three-clan penalty."
proposals.after: During the siege of Chengdu, Liu Bei ordered: "Anyone who harms Liu Ba will answer with the three-clan penalty."
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses Chengdu with Liu Bei and yields a false compound name.

proposals.before: Is he only passing through on his way north, or does he mean to help me at all?"
proposals.after: He wants to return north and is only borrowing a road here—does he mean to complete my enterprise?"
proposals.reason: The Chinese states a desire to return north and borrow the road, then asks whether that completes Bei’s enterprise; the idiomatic version turns this into an either-or travel question.

proposals.before: 〈Pei Songzhi thinks Ma Liang may have sworn brotherhood with Zhuge Liang or been related by marriage;
proposals.after: 〈Pei Songzhi thinks Ma Liang may have sworn brotherhood with Zhuge Liang or been related by kinship;
proposals.reason: Chinese 有親 means kinship in general, not specifically marriage.

proposals.before: When ruler and ministers temper brilliance and win the distant, when virtue spans heaven and earth so that the age may hear clearly and the world cleaves to the Way—when lofty melody sets vulgar music right and every part serves the whole without throwing off the ensemble—that is the perfection Shi Kuang knew at his harp.
proposals.after: When ruler and ministers temper brilliance and win the distant, when virtue spans heaven and earth so that the age may hear clearly and the world cleaves to the Way—when lofty melody sets vulgar music right and every part serves the whole without throwing off the ensemble—that is the perfection of strings and winds, the tuning of Bo Ya and Shi Kuang.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 牙 (Bo Ya) and collapses 牙、曠 into Shi Kuang alone.

proposals.before: As for blending radiance and pleasing the distant, spanning virtue between Heaven and earth, causing the age to find leisure in listening and the generation to submit to the Way, aligning tones that are lofty and subtle and correcting sounds like those of Zheng and Wei—together benefiting affairs without mutual violation of proper order—this is the perfection of strings and winds, the tuning of Ya [Shi Kuang] and Kuang [Musician Kuang].
proposals.after: As for blending radiance and pleasing the distant, spanning virtue between Heaven and earth, causing the age to find leisure in listening and the generation to submit to the Way, aligning tones that are lofty and subtle and correcting sounds like those of Zheng and Wei—together benefiting affairs without mutual violation of proper order—this is the perfection of strings and winds, the tuning of Ya [Bo Ya] and Kuang [Shi Kuang].
proposals.reason: Glosses reverse the identifications: 牙 is Bo Ya and 曠 is Shi Kuang.

proposals.before: Liu Bei posthumously appointed Ma Liang’s son Bing chief commandant of cavalry.
proposals.after: Liu Bei appointed Ma Liang’s son Bing chief commandant of cavalry.
proposals.reason: Chinese 拜 is an ordinary appointment of the son after the father's death; it does not say the appointment was posthumous.

proposals.before: Zhuge Liang took the advice, repeatedly sparing Meng Huo until the south submitted.
proposals.after: Zhuge Liang took the advice and pardoned Meng Huo in order to subdue the south.
proposals.reason: Chinese 赦孟獲 states a pardon, not repeated sparings; the seven-captures legend is not in this unit.

proposals.before: There were five brothers, all having talent and reputation; the village made for them a proverb, saying: 'The Ma family's Five Changs—the white eyebrow is the finest Liang.'
proposals.after: There were five brothers, all having talent and reputation; the village made for them a proverb, saying: 'The Ma family's Five Changs—the white eyebrow is the finest.'
proposals.reason: 最良 means finest/best; inserting Liang as if the proverb already names him over-translates the pun.

proposals.before: Ma Liang died at thirty-six; Ma Su was executed at thirty-nine.
proposals.after: Ma Liang died at thirty-six; Ma Su died at thirty-nine.
proposals.reason: Chinese 謖年三十九 only states Su's age at death; execution is not in this sentence (s0131 has 物故, death in prison).

proposals.before: In the seventh year [229], Sun Quan assumed the honored title; he appointed Zhen as Commandant of the Guards to congratulate Quan on ascending the throne. Zhuge Liang wrote to his elder brother Jin, saying: 'Xiaoqi's nature is loyal and pure; in old age it grows ever more earnest; as for his assisting narrative east and west, joy and harmony unite—there is something admirable in this.'
proposals.after: In the seventh year [229], Sun Quan assumed the honored title; [the Shu court] appointed Zhen as Commandant of the Guards to congratulate Quan on ascending the throne. Zhuge Liang wrote to his elder brother Jin, saying: 'Xiaoqi's nature is loyal and pure; in old age it grows ever more earnest; as for his assisting narrative east and west, joy and harmony unite—there is something admirable in this.'
proposals.reason: 以震為衛尉賀權踐阼 is Shu sending Chen Zhen with the Guard Commandant title to congratulate Sun Quan, not Sun Quan appointing him.

proposals.before: Before Zhuge Liang marched north from Hanzhong he worried that the young emperor could not tell sound counsel from flattery; Dong Yun’s integrity made him the right man for palace oversight.
proposals.after: When Zhuge Liang was about to campaign north and was stationed in Hanzhong, he worried that the young emperor could not tell sound counsel from flattery; Dong Yun’s integrity made him the right man for palace oversight.
proposals.reason: Chinese 將北征，住漢中 means he was about to campaign north and lodged in Hanzhong, not that he marched north from Hanzhong.

proposals.before: If they offer no words that advance virtue, then punish Yun and the others to make their negligence plain.'
proposals.after: If they offer no words that advance virtue, then execute Yun and the others to make their negligence plain.'
proposals.reason: 戮 means execute, not a milder punish.

proposals.before: 〈The Chu tradition describes Guo Youzhi of Nanyang as a man of recognized ability.〉
proposals.after: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Chu states: Youzhi was a man of Nanyang; he was known in his time for capacity and achievement.〉
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English collapses 楚國先賢傳 into 'Chu tradition' and omits the stated native place plus contemporary reputation.

proposals.before: 〈Chang Qu’s Huayang guozhi reports that Shu folk grouped Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and Dong Yun as the “four excellences.”〉
proposals.after: 〈The Records of Huayang states: At that time the people of Shu regarded Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and Yun as the four chancellors, also called the Four Heroes.〉
proposals.reason: Chinese names the book 華陽國志 only; Chang Qu is not in the source, and 四相 / 四英 are chancellors and heroes rather than a single 'four excellences.'

proposals.before: Chen Shou comments: Dong He embodied the integrity praised in the “Lamb” ode; Liu Ba kept himself unstained; Ma Liang was upright and rightly called a model scholar; Chen Zhen grew only more loyal with age; Dong Yun rebuked his sovereign without masking his anger—they were Shu’s finest servants.
proposals.after: The appraisal states: Dong He embodied the integrity praised in the “Lamb” ode; Liu Ba kept himself unstained; Ma Liang was upright and rightly called a model scholar; Chen Zhen grew only more loyal with age; Dong Yun rebuked his sovereign without masking his anger—they were Shu’s finest servants.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 評曰 does not name Chen Shou; the idiomatic line invents an explicit speaker the source leaves as the historian’s appraisal formula.

proposals.before: Lü Yi when overseeing commanderies hung forth praise; when dwelling at court suffered diminishment—he also is of the subordinate stream of Huang [Ba] and Xue [Xuan Gong].
proposals.after: Lü Yi when overseeing commanderies won praise; when dwelling at court suffered diminishment—he also is of the lesser stream of Huang Ba and Xue Xuan.
proposals.reason: The bracketed reconstructions and hung forth praise are opaque; the conventional Han pair is Huang Ba and Xue Xuan, and 垂稱 means his reputation spread.

decisions.reason: 軍師將軍 is Zhuge Liang’s Army Advisor General office; “Military Director-in-Chief” invents an in-chief rank the title does not carry, and the replacement names the same office accurately without other changes.

decisions.after: I would blush before the maxim ‘to possess yet seem empty, to be full yet seem modest’—I cannot accept this honor!"〉
decisions.reason: The speech ends at 何以堪之, so the extra English quote after the commentary closer is an artifact. The proposal also drops the source’s 〉 closer, which this chapter’s commentary lines retain.

decisions.after: When Liu Bei came to occupy the three commanderies, Liu Ba could not return from his mission, so he went far toward Jiaozhi.
decisions.reason: 會先主略有三郡，巴不得反使 states coincidence and an unfinished envoy return, not a cutoff of a road, and 遠適 is travel rather than flight. The proposal restores that sense but is awkward and needlessly swaps the chapter’s idiomatic Liu Bei for First Sovereign.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 會先主略有三郡，巴不得反使，遂遠適交阯

decisions.reason: From Jiaozhi Liu Ba is ordinary English for 巴復從交阯至蜀; the missing comma does not fuse the place and the person into a false name, so the change is only stylistic.
During the siege of Chengdu Liu Bei ordered already matches 備攻成都，令軍中曰; Chengdu and Liu Bei do not read as one name, so the added comma is stylistic.

其欲還北，假道於此 is a statement that he wants to go north and is borrowing the road, followed by 豈欲成孤事邪; the original turns that into an either-or travel question and loses the charge about completing Bei’s enterprise.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其欲還北，假道於此，豈欲成孤事邪

decisions.reason: 或相與有親 is kinship in general; the original’s “related by marriage” narrows 親 to a relation the Chinese does not specify.
此乃管弦之至，牙、曠之調也 names both 牙 (Bo Ya) and 曠 (Shi Kuang) as the standard of strings and winds; the original drops Bo Ya and collapses the pair into Shi Kuang alone.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此乃管弦之至，牙、曠之調也

decisions.reason: 牙、曠 is Bo Ya then Shi Kuang; the original glosses reverse the identifications and even make Kuang a second “Musician Kuang.”
先主拜良子秉為騎都尉 is an ordinary appointment of the living son after Ma Liang’s death; 拜 does not mark the office as posthumous.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 先主拜良子秉為騎都尉

decisions.reason: 亮納其策，赦孟獲以服南方 records one pardon used to subdue the south; “repeatedly sparing” imports the seven-captures story, which is not in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 亮納其策，赦孟獲以服南方

decisions.reason: The proverb is 白眉最良; 最良 means finest, and inserting Liang inside the quoted rhyme over-translates the pun as if the saying already named him.
謖年三十九 only gives Su’s age at death in parallel with 良死時年三十六; execution is not in this sentence, and the adjoining 下獄物故 is death in prison, not a named execution.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 良死時年三十六，謖年三十九

decisions.reason: After 孫權稱尊號, 以震為衛尉賀權踐阼 is Shu making Zhen Guard Commandant to congratulate Quan’s accession; taking 孫權 as the subject who appointed him reverses the agent.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孫權稱尊號，以震為衛尉，賀權踐阼

decisions.reason: 將北征，住漢中 is impending northern campaign while stationed in Hanzhong; “marched north from Hanzhong” treats the lodging as already a departure from that base.
則戮允等以彰其慢 uses 戮, to put to death, not a milder generic punish; the replacement matches the verb without changing the rest of the memorial line.
The original already places Guo Youzhi in Nanyang and as a man of recognized ability, which covers 南陽人 and 以器業知名於時; expanding 楚國先賢傳 from “Chu tradition” is stylistic, not a semantic error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 攸之，南陽人，以器業知名於時

decisions.reason: The note cites 《華陽國志》 only and distinguishes 四相 from 一號四英; naming Chang Qu and collapsing both labels into “four excellences” adds an author the unit does not name and erases the two designations.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時蜀人以諸葛亮、蔣琬、費禕及允為四相，一號四英也

decisions.reason: 評曰 is the historian’s appraisal formula and does not name Chen Shou; “Chen Shou comments” invents an explicit speaker the Chinese leaves unnamed.
黃、薛 is the Han pair Huang Ba and Xue Xuan; the gloss Xue [Xuan Gong] garbles that identification, and 垂稱 is reputation won or spread, not the opaque calque “hung forth praise.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 呂乂臨郡則垂稱，處朝則被損，亦黃、薛之流亞矣
